akhfash:8-9.t: He said ﴿فَأَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَيْمَنَةِ مَآ أَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَيْمَنَةِ﴾ ﴿وَأَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَشْأَمَةِ مَآ أَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَشْأَمَةِ﴾: His word ﴿مَآ أَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَشْأَمَةِ﴾ is the khabar (predicate). The Arabs say: "زيدٌ وَمَا زيدٌ" (Zayd — and what is Zayd!), meaning "Zayd is formidable".

akhfash:16-16.t: And He said ﴿مُّتَّكِئِينَ عَلَيْهَا مُتَقَابِلِينَ﴾ by way of praise; he put it in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), meaning: "they have this, reclining".

akhfash:26-26.t: And He said ﴿إِلاَّ قِيلاً سَلاَماً سَلاَماً﴾: if you wish you put "salām" in the accusative by "the saying" (القيل); if you wish you make "salām" conjoined to "the saying", as though it were an explanation of it; and if you wish you make the verb operate on "salām", meaning "they hear nothing but a saying — the good", i.e. except that they say the good, and salām is the good.

akhfash:35-37.t: And He said ﴿إِنَّآ أَنشَأْنَاهُنَّ إِنشَآءً فَجَعَلْنَاهُنَّ أَبْكَاراً عُرُباً أَتْرَاباً﴾: He referred to them by a pronoun without having mentioned them before that. As for "الأَترابُ" (those of equal age), its singular is "التِرْبَ", and for the feminine "التِربَة": "she is my contemporary" (هي تِربى, هي تِرْبَتي), like "شِبْه" and "أَشْباه" (likeness, likenesses). Both "التِرْبُ" and "التِرْبَةُ" are allowed for the feminine, and it is pluralised as "الأَتْراب", just as you say "حَيَّةٌ" and "أَحْياء" (living) when you mean a woman, and "مَيْتَةٌ" and "أَمْواتٌ" (dead).

akhfash:53-54.t: And He said ﴿فَمَالِئُونَ مِنْهَا ٱلْبُطُونَ﴾, i.e. from the tree, ﴿فَشَارِبُونَ عَلَيْهِ﴾, because "الشَجَر" (trees) is feminine and masculine. He used the feminine because He construed it on "الشَجَرة" (the tree), since "الشجرةَ" can indicate the collective. The Arabs say: "نَبَتَتَ قِبَلَنا شَجَرةٌ مُرَّةٌ وَبَقْلَةٌ رذية" (a bitter tree and a poor herb grew in our parts), and they mean the collective.

akhfash:55-55.t: [And] He said ﴿فَشَارِبُونَ شُرْبَ﴾, and ﴿شُرْبَ﴾ (with fatḥa), like "الضَّعْف" and "الضُّعْف" (weakness).

akhfash:73-73.t: And He said ﴿مَتَاعاً لِّلْمُقْوِينَ﴾, i.e. for travellers in the desolate land (القِيِّ). You say: "أَقْوَى الشيءُ" when everything in it has gone.

akhfash:83-83.t: And He said ﴿فَلَوْلاَ إِذَا بَلَغَتِ ٱلْحُلْقُومَ﴾, then He said ﴿فَلَوْلاَ إِن كُنتُمْ غَيْرَ مَدِينِينَ﴾, i.e. not requited, subdued — (why do) you (not) bring back that soul while you see how it departs at that time, ﴿إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ that you can hold yourselves back from death? Then He informed them, saying ﴿فَأَمَّآ إِن كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبِينَ﴾ ﴿فَرَوْحٌ وَرَيْحَانٌ﴾, i.e. for him is rest and fragrance; ﴿وَأَمَّآ إِن كَانَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ ٱلْيَمِينِ﴾ ﴿فَسَلاَمٌ لَّكَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ ٱلْيَمِينِ﴾, i.e. it will be said to him: "peace be to you".

akhfash:95-95.t: And He said ﴿حَقُّ ٱلْيَقِينِ﴾: He annexed (حقّ) to "اليَقِينِ" (the certain), as He said ﴿دِينُ ٱلقَيِّمَةِ﴾, i.e. that is the religion of the upright creed, and that is the truth of the certain matter. As for "هذا رَجُلُ السَوْءِ" (this is a man of evil), one cannot say in it "هذا الرجلُ السَوْءُ" (this man, the evil), as one can in "الحقُّ اليَقِينُ" (the certain truth), because "السَّوْءَ" (evil) is not "الرَّجُلِ" (the man), whereas the certain is the truth.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverbial (ẓarfiyya), non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿وَقَعَتِ الْواقِعَةُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿لَيْسَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿لِوَقْعَتِها﴾ the fronted khabar (predicate) of ليس. ﴿كاذِبَةٌ﴾ its postponed noun (ism); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿خافِضَةٌ﴾ khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿رافِعَةٌ﴾ a second khabar; the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya).

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿إِذا﴾ a badal (substitute) from the preceding one. ﴿رُجَّتِ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿الْأَرْضُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿رَجًّا﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:5-5.t: Its i'rab is like that of the preceding verse, and it is conjoined to it.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿فَكانَتْ﴾ kāna, and its noun (ism) is latent (mustatir). ﴿هَباءً﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿مُنْبَثًّا﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of هباء; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وَكُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun (ism). ﴿أَزْواجاً﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿ثَلاثَةً﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of أزواجا; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿فَأَصْحابُ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and أصحاب is a mubtadaʾ (subject), annexed to الميمنة. ﴿الْمَيْمَنَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿ما﴾ interrogative, a second mubtadaʾ, and أصحاب is the khabar (predicate) of ما, and it is muḍāf. ﴿الْمَيْمَنَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the khabar of أصحاب, and the clause أصحاب.. is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:9-9.t: Its i'rab is like that of the preceding verse, and it is conjoined to it.

daas-irab:10-10.t: A mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. [Translator's note: the verse is ﴿وَالسَّابِقُونَ السَّابِقُونَ﴾.]

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿أُولئِكَ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the clause is a second khabar of السابقون.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿فِي جَنَّاتِ﴾ a second khabar (predicate) of أولئك. ﴿النَّعِيمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿ثُلَّةٌ﴾ khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مِنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of ثلة.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿وَقَلِيلٌ﴾ conjoined to ثلة. ﴿مِنَ الْآخِرِينَ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) قليل.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿عَلى سُرُرٍ﴾ a second ṣifa (adjective) of ثلة. ﴿مَوْضُونَةٍ﴾ a ṣifa of سرر.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), and ﴿عَلَيْها﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them. ﴿مُتَقابِلِينَ﴾ a second ḥāl.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿يَطُوفُ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وِلْدانٌ﴾ fāʿil (agent). ﴿مُخَلَّدُونَ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿بِأَكْوابٍ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) يطوف. ﴿وَأَبارِيقَ﴾ conjoined to أكواب. ﴿وَكَأْسٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مِنْ مَعِينٍ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of كأس.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يُصَدَّعُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿عَنْها﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿وَلا﴾ negative. ﴿يُنْزِفُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿وَفاكِهَةٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مِمَّا﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of فاكهة. ﴿يَتَخَيَّرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما.

daas-irab:21-21.t: The verse is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿وَحُورٌ﴾ conjoined to ولدان. ﴿عِينٌ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of حور.

daas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿كَأَمْثالِ﴾ a second ṣifa (adjective) of حور. ﴿اللُّؤْلُؤِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الْمَكْنُونِ﴾ a ṣifa of اللؤلؤ.

daas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿جَزاءً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) جزاء. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun (ism); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of كانوا.

daas-irab:25-25.t: ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَسْمَعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فِيها﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿لَغْواً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and لا is negative. ﴿تَأْثِيماً﴾ conjoined to لغوا.

daas-irab:26-26.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception. ﴿قِيلًا﴾ excepted by إلا, accusative (manṣūb). ﴿سَلاماً﴾ a badal (substitute) from قيلا. ﴿سَلاماً﴾ tawkīd (emphasis).

daas-irab:27-27.t: Identical to the i'rab of verse no. 8.

daas-irab:28-28.t: ﴿فِي سِدْرٍ﴾ a second khabar (predicate) of أصحاب. ﴿مَخْضُودٍ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of سدر.

daas-irab:33-33.t: ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿مَقْطُوعَةٍ﴾ a second ṣifa (adjective) of فاكهة. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and لا is negative. ﴿مَمْنُوعَةٍ﴾ conjoined to مقطوعة.

daas-irab:34-34.t: ﴿فُرُشٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مَرْفُوعَةٍ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of فرش.

daas-irab:35-35.t: ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun (ism). ﴿أَنْشَأْناهُنَّ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of إن. ﴿إِنْشاءً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:36-36.t: ﴿فَجَعَلْناهُنَّ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first object. ﴿أَبْكاراً﴾ its second object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:38-38.t: ﴿لِأَصْحابِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to (mutaʿalliq) جعلناهن. ﴿الْيَمِينِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:39-39.t: ﴿ثُلَّةٌ﴾ khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مِنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of ثلة; the clause is a ṣifa of أصحاب.

daas-irab:41-41.t: The i'rab of its counterpart has preceded in verse 8.

daas-irab:42-42.t: ﴿فِي سَمُومٍ﴾ a second khabar (predicate) of أصحاب الشمال. ﴿وَحَمِيمٍ﴾ conjoined to سموم.

daas-irab:44-44.t: ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿بارِدٍ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of ظل. ﴿وَلا كَرِيمٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:45-45.t: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ inna and its noun (ism). ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿قَبْلَ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of time. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مُتْرَفِينَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of كانوا; the clause كانوا.. is the khabar of إنهم, and the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:46-46.t: ﴿وَكانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun (ism). ﴿يُصِرُّونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of كانوا. ﴿عَلَى الْحِنْثِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْعَظِيمِ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of الحنث; the clause كانوا.. is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:47-47.t:
﴿وَكانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun (ism). ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of كانوا, and the clause كانوا..
is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَإِذا﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and إذا is an adverbial (ẓarfiyya), non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿مِتْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿وَكُنَّا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿تُراباً﴾ its khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَعِظاماً﴾ conjoined to ترابا. ﴿أَإِنَّا﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and inna and its noun. ﴿لَمَبْعُوثُونَ﴾ the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and مبعوثون is its khabar; the nominal clause emphasises what precedes it.

daas-irab:48-48.t: ﴿أَوَآباؤُنَا﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, the wāw is a conjunction, and آباؤنا is conjoined to the latent (mustatir) pronoun in لمبعوثون. ﴿الْأَوَّلُونَ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective).

daas-irab:49-49.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir). ﴿إِنَّ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ inna and its noun (ism). ﴿وَالْآخِرِينَ﴾ conjoined to الأولين.

daas-irab:50-50.t: ﴿لَمَجْمُوعُونَ﴾ the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and مجموعون is the khabar (predicate) of إن, nominative with the wāw; the nominal clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying), and the clause قل.. is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِلى مِيقاتِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) مجموعون. ﴿يَوْمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مَعْلُومٍ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of يوم.

daas-irab:51-51.t: ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿إِنَّكُمْ﴾ inna and its noun (ism). ﴿أَيُّهَا﴾ the one addressed in the vocative (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda). ﴿الضَّالُّونَ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of أيّ. ﴿الْمُكَذِّبُونَ﴾ a second ṣifa of the omitted qualified noun; the vocative clause is parenthetical, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:52-52.t: ﴿لَآكِلُونَ﴾ the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and آكلون is the khabar (predicate) of إن. ﴿مِنْ شَجَرٍ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) آكلون. ﴿مِنْ زَقُّومٍ﴾ a badal (substitute) from what precedes it; the clause إنكم is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:53-53.t: ﴿فَمالِؤُنَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and مالئون is conjoined to آكلون. ﴿مِنْهَا﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) مالئون. ﴿الْبُطُونَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle.

daas-irab:54-54.t: ﴿فَشارِبُونَ﴾ شاربون is conjoined to آكلون. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) شاربون. ﴿مِنَ﴾ الحميم: both attached to شاربون.

daas-irab:55-55.t: ﴿فَشارِبُونَ﴾ شاربون is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿شُرْبَ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿الْهِيمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:56-56.t: ﴿هذا نُزُلُهُمْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. يوم is an adverb (ẓarf) of time, annexed to الدين.

daas-irab:57-57.t: ﴿نَحْنُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿خَلَقْناكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَلَوْلا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and لولا is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). ﴿تُصَدِّقُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:58-58.t: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿ما﴾ first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿تُمْنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and the clause أفرأيتم.. is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:59-59.t: ﴿أَأَنْتُمْ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿تَخْلُقُونَهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is its object; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of رأيتم. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿نَحْنُ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْخالِقُونَ﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:60-60.t: ﴿نَحْنُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿قَدَّرْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿بَيْنَكُمُ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of place. ﴿الْمَوْتَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and ما is negative, operating like ليس. ﴿نَحْنُ﴾ its noun (ism). ﴿بِمَسْبُوقِينَ﴾ genitive in form by the redundant (zāʾida) bāʾ, accusative in position as the khabar of ما; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:61-61.t:
﴿عَلى﴾
a preposition. ﴿أَنْ نُبَدِّلَ﴾
an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) مسبوقين. ﴿أَمْثالَكُمْ﴾
mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَنُنْشِئَكُمْ﴾
an imperfect verb conjoined to نبدل. ﴿فِي ما﴾
both attached to what precedes them. ﴿لا﴾
negative. ﴿تَعْلَمُونَ﴾
an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:62-62.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive [Translator's note: so in the source; the wāw here is generally parsed as resumptive, with the oath implied], the lām occurs in the response to the oath, and قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿عَلِمْتُمُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿النَّشْأَةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الْأُولى﴾ a ṣifa (adjective); the clause is the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), with no grammatical position. ﴿فَلَوْلا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and لولا is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). ﴿تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:63-63.t: The i'rab of its like has gone before.

daas-irab:64-64.t: The i'rab of its like has gone before.

daas-irab:65-65.t: ﴿لَوْ﴾ a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿نَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿لَجَعَلْناهُ﴾ the lām occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and a past verb, its fāʿil and its first object. ﴿حُطاماً﴾ its second object; the clause is the apodosis, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَظَلْتُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the tāʾ is its noun (ism). ﴿تَفَكَّهُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of ظلتم, conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:66-66.t: ﴿إِنَّا لَمُغْرَمُونَ﴾ inna and its noun (ism), the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and مغرمون is its khabar (predicate); the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying) of an omitted saying.

daas-irab:67-67.t: ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction. ﴿نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:68-68.t: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْماءَ﴾ its object; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of الماء. ﴿تَشْرَبُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:69-69.t: ﴿أَأَنْتُمْ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿أَنْزَلْتُمُوهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object. ﴿مِنَ الْمُزْنِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of أرأيتم. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿نَحْنُ الْمُنْزِلُونَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:70-70.t: ﴿لَوْ نَشاءُ جَعَلْناهُ أُجاجاً﴾ the i'rab of its counterpart has gone before. ﴿فَلَوْلا تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ its i'rab has preceded.

daas-irab:71-71.t: The i'rab of its like has gone before.

daas-irab:72-72.t: The i'rab of its like has gone before.

daas-irab:73-73.t: ﴿نَحْنُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿جَعَلْناها﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿تَذْكِرَةً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَمَتاعاً﴾ conjoined to تذكرة. ﴿لِلْمُقْوِينَ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) متاعا; the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:74-74.t: ﴿فَسَبِّحْ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition), and an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿بِاسْمِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الْعَظِيمِ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of ربك.

daas-irab:75-75.t: ﴿فَلا أُقْسِمُ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, لا is negative, and an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir). ﴿بِمَواقِعِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿النُّجُومِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:76-76.t: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ﴾ the wāw is parenthetical, and inna and its noun (ism). ﴿لَقَسَمٌ﴾ the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and قسم is its khabar (predicate); the clause is parenthetical, with no grammatical position. ﴿لَوْ﴾ a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿عَظِيمٌ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of قسم.

daas-irab:77-77.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ لَقُرْآنٌ﴾ inna and its noun (ism), the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and قرآن is its khabar (predicate). ﴿كَرِيمٌ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective); the clause is the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:78-78.t: ﴿فِي كِتابٍ﴾ في كتاب is a second ṣifa (adjective) of قرآن. ﴿مَكْنُونٍ﴾ a ṣifa of كتاب.

daas-irab:79-79.t: ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَمَسُّهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is a third ṣifa (adjective) of قرآن.

daas-irab:80-80.t: ﴿تَنْزِيلٌ﴾ also a ṣifa (adjective) of قرآن. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّ﴾ a ṣifa of تنزيل. ﴿الْعالَمِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:81-81.t: ﴿أَفَبِهذَا﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿بهذا﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) مدهنون. ﴿الْحَدِيثِ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of the demonstrative. ﴿أَنْتُمْ مُدْهِنُونَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:82-82.t: ﴿وَتَجْعَلُونَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿رِزْقَكُمْ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿أَنَّكُمْ﴾ anna and its noun (ism). ﴿تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of أنكم, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and what follows it is the second mafʿūl bihi of تجعلون; the clause تجعلون is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:83-83.t: ﴿فَلَوْلا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, لولا is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ), and إذا is merely adverbial (ẓarfiyya). ﴿بَلَغَتِ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿الْحُلْقُومَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

daas-irab:84-84.t: ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿حِينَئِذٍ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) annexed to its like. ﴿تَنْظُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is circumstantial.

daas-irab:85-85.t: ﴿وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) أقرب. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ both attached to أقرب. ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and لكن is lightened and inoperative (mukhaffafa muhmala). ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿تُبْصِرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:86-86.t: ﴿فَلَوْلا﴾ conjoined to its like. ﴿إِنْ﴾ a jussive conditional particle. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun (ism). ﴿غَيْرَ﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿مَدِينِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:87-87.t: ﴿تَرْجِعُونَها﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun (ism). ﴿صادِقِينَ﴾ its khabar (predicate); the clause كنتم is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position, and the apodosis is omitted.

daas-irab:88-88.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and أما is a particle of condition and detailing (sharṭ wa-tafṣīl). ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional. ﴿كانَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun (ism) latent (mustatir). ﴿مِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of كان; the verbal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:89-89.t: ﴿فَرَوْحٌ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the response (jawāb) of أما, and روح is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted; the nominal clause is the response of أما. ﴿وَرَيْحانٌ وَجَنَّةُ﴾ both conjoined to روح. ﴿نَعِيمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:90-90.t: Conjoined to what precedes it, and the i'rab is the same.

daas-irab:91-91.t: ﴿فَسَلامٌ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the response (jawāb) of أما, and سلام is a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لَكَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is the response of أما, with no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ أَصْحابِ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿الْيَمِينِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:92-92.t: The i'rab of its like has gone before.

daas-irab:93-93.t: ﴿فَنُزُلٌ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the response (jawāb) of أما, and نزل is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted; the clause is the response of أما, with no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ حَمِيمٍ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of نزل.

daas-irab:94-94.t: ﴿وَتَصْلِيَةُ﴾ conjoined to نزل, and it is muḍāf. ﴿جَحِيمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:95-95.t: ﴿إِنَّ هذا﴾ inna and its noun (ism). ﴿لَهُوَ﴾ the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and هو is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿حَقُّ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of إن. ﴿الْيَقِينِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِهَا كَاذِبَةٌ﴾.
He is saying: there is no turning it back and no repelling it. «الكاذبة» here is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like «العاقبة» (outcome) and «العافية» (well-being).
He said: Abū Tharwān said to me in his speech: «إن بنى نمير ليس لحدهم مكذوبة» (the Banū Numayr — there is no belying their edge), meaning: belying. Then He said: ﴿خافِضَةٌ رافِعةٌ﴾ as a new sentence (istiʾnāf), that is: the Event on that day will be lowering one people into the Fire and raising another people into Paradise. Had a reader read «خافضةً رافعةً» (accusative), meaning: when it happens, lowering some people and raising others, (it would be possible); but it is ugly, because the Arabs do not say «إذا أتيتى زائراً» (when you come to me visiting) until they say: «إذا أتيتنى فأتنى زائراً» (when you come to me, come to me visiting) or «ائتنى زائراً». But it is good in al-Wāqiʿa, because before the accusative there is a verse on which it is good to pause, so the implied (verb) becomes good in what begins anew.
«[Translator's note: «أتيتى» is as printed, evidently for «أتيتنى».]»

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿إِذَا رُجَّتِ ٱلأَرْضُ رَجّاً﴾.
When it is shaken until every building on the face of the earth collapses.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿وَبُسَّتِ ٱلْجِبَالُ بَسّاً﴾.
They become like flour; and that is His saying: ﴿وَسُيِّرَتِ الْجِبالُ﴾. I heard the Arabs recite:
لا تَخْبِزا خَبْزا وبُسّا بَسّا * مَلْسا بذَوْدا لحلَسِّ مَلْسا
(Do not bake bread, but mix (the meal) quickly, and drive the camels on swiftly.)
والحُمّسِ أيضا
And «البسيسة» among them is flour, or barley-meal (sawīq) that is moistened and taken as provision.
«[Translator's note: the second half-verse and the words «والحمس أيضا» are garbled in the printed text; the gloss renders the sense of the commonly cited verse «لا تخبزا خبزا وبسا بسا * ولا تطيلا بمناخ حبسا».]»

farraa:7-11.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكُنتُمْ أَزْوَاجاً ثَلاَثَةً ﴾; then He explained them, saying: ﴿فَأَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَيْمَنَةِ مَآ أَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَيْمَنَةِ﴾.
He made His Prophet wonder at them, saying: what are the companions of the right? What kind of people are they? They are the companions of the right hand. ﴿وَأَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَشْأَمَةِ مَآ أَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَشْأَمَةِ﴾: He made him wonder at them too; they are the companions of the left hand. Then He said: ﴿وَٱلسَّابِقُونَ ٱلسَّابِقُونَ﴾. This is the third class. If you wish, you make «السابقين» nominative by the second «السابقين» (i.e. as mubtadaʾ and khabar); they are the Emigrants (al-Muhājirūn), and everyone who was first (to believe) in one of the prophets is among these. If you make one of them nominative by the other, it is like your saying «الأول السابق» (the first is the foremost). And if you wish, you make the second an emphasis of the first, and it is made nominative by His saying: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبُونَ﴾.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مَّوْضُونَةٍ﴾.
«موضونة» means woven. The Arabs only called the she-camel's girth «وضين» because it is woven. I have heard one of the Arabs say: «فإذا الآجر موضون بعضه على بعض» (and the bricks were laid closely one upon another), meaning: fitted together. [Al-Farrāʾ said: «الوضين» is the girth.]

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿وِلْدَانٌ مُّخَلَّدُونَ﴾.
It is said that they are of one age and do not change. The Arabs say of a man who has grown old without his hair turning grey: «إنه لمخلّد»; and when his teeth have not gone with old age, it is also said: «إنه لمخلّد». It is also said: «مخلّدون» means wearing earrings; and it is said: wearing bracelets.

farraa:18-18.t:
[191/ا] His saying: ﴿بِأَكْوَابٍ وَأَبَارِيقَ﴾.
«الكوب» is (a vessel) that has neither a spout (lit. ear) nor a handle; and «الأباريق» are those with spouts and handles.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَّ يُصَدَّعُونَ عَنْهَا﴾: from the wine; ﴿وَلاَ يُنزِفُونَ﴾: that is, their minds will not go.
It is said of a man when he is drunk: «قد نُزِف عقله» (his mind has been drained); and when his blood has gone and he has fainted or died, it is said: «منزوف».
Whoever reads "يُنْزِفون" is saying: their wine will not run out. The Arabs say of people when their provisions have run out: «قد أنْزَفُوا» (they have run dry), «أقتروا», «أنفضوا», «أرمَلوا» and «أملقوا».

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿وَحُورٍ عِينٍ﴾.
The companions of ʿAbd Allāh read it in the genitive, and that is the proper Arabic construction, even though most readers are for the nominative. (The latter) were wary of making the wide-eyed houris be "carried round" (yuṭāf bihinna), so they put them in the nominative, as in your saying: «and they have wide-eyed houris», or «with them are wide-eyed houris». The genitive is on the basis that you make the end of the statement follow its beginning, even if what is good in its beginning is not good in its end. One of the Arabs recited to me:
إذا ما الغانيات بَرَزْنَ يَوْماً * وزَجّجن الحواجب والعيونا
(When the fair women come out one day, having pencilled their eyebrows and eyes.)
The eye is not pencilled (with zajj); it is only lined with kohl; but he conjoined it to the eyebrows because the meaning is understood. Another recited to me:
ولقيتُ زوجك فى الوغى * متقلداً سيفاً ورمحاً
(I met your husband in battle, girded with a sword and a spear.)
A spear is not girded on; but he conjoined it to the sword. Another said:
تسمع للأحشاء منه لغطاً * ولليدين جُسْأَةً وبَدَدا
(You hear a clamour from his insides, and (see) stiffness and wide spread in his forelegs.)
One of Banū Dubayr recited to me:
علفتها تِبناً وماءً بارداً * حتى شَتَتْ همالةً عيناها
(I fed her straw and cool water, until she spent the winter with her eyes streaming.)
Water is not fed as fodder; it is only drunk; but he made it follow «التبن». Whoever read «وحورٌ عين» because — so he claimed — they are not carried round, ought to have said "وفاكهةٌ ولَحْم طير" as well, because fruit and meat are not carried round either; only wine is carried round. So there is a clear indication in that, for the genitive is the proper construction of the speech. In the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb it is «وحورا عيناً», intending the verb that you find (implied) in speech like this, as in the poet's saying:
جئنى بمثل بنى بَدْرٍ لقومهم * أو مثلَ أسرة منظور بن سيار
(Bring me the like of the Banū Badr for their people, or the like of the family of Manẓūr ibn Sayyār.)

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ قِيلاً سَلاَماً سَلاَماً﴾.
If you wish, you make «السلام» follow «القيل» (as badal), it being the same thing; and if you wish, you mean «إلاّ قيلَ سلامٍ سلامٍ». When you give it nunation, you put it in the accusative because the verb falls upon it. Had it been nominative — «قيلا سلامٌ سلامٌ» — it would have been permissible.
One of the Arabs, al-ʿUqaylī, recited to me:
فقلنا السلام فاتقت من أميرها * فَما كان إلا ومؤها بالحواجب
(We said "Peace!", and she was wary of her guardian, so there was nothing but her signalling with her eyebrows.)
He meant to quote the one who begins with the greeting. Al-Kisāʾī heard the Arabs say: «التقينا فقلنا: سلام سلام، ثم تفرقنا» (we met and said "Peace, peace", then we parted); he meant: we said "Peace be upon you", and they returned it to us.
«[Translator's note: «العقبلى» in the source is evidently a misprint for «العقيلى»; rendered as al-ʿUqaylī.]»

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿فِي سِدْرٍ مَّخْضُودٍ﴾.
With no thorns in it.

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿وَطَلْحٍ مَّنضُودٍ﴾.
Al-Kalbī mentioned that it is the banana; and it is said: it is the ṭalḥ (acacia) that you know.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿وَظِلٍّ مَّمْدُودٍ﴾.
With no sun in it, like the shade between the break [191/ب] of dawn and sunrise.

farraa:32-33.t:
His saying: ﴿وَفَاكِهَةٍ كَثِيرَةٍ لاَّ مَقْطُوعَةٍ وَلاَ مَمْنُوعَةٍ﴾.
It does not come at one time and cease at another; it is always constant; «ولا ممنوعة»: (nor withheld) as the owners of orchards withhold their fruits.

farraa:34-34.t:
His saying: ﴿وَفُرُشٍ مَّرْفُوعَةٍ﴾.
Some above others.

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّآ أَنشَأْنَاهُنَّ إِنشَآءً﴾.
He is saying: We re-created the young girl and the old woman and made them of equal age, thirty-three years old.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿عُرُباً﴾.
Its singular is «عَروب»: the woman who shows her love to her husband, the coquettish.
Al-Farrāʾ told us: an elder told me, from al-Aʿmash, who said: I used to hear them read "عُرْباً أتراباً" with the light form (sukūn). It is like your saying «الرسْل» and «الكتْب» in the dialect of Tamīm and Bakr, with the light form; but the heavy form (with ḍamma) is the proper reading, because every «فعول», «فعيل» or «فِعال» that is pluralised on this pattern is heavy, whether masculine or feminine, and the readers follow that.
«[Translator's note: «ولتثقيل» is as printed, evidently for «والتثقيل».]»

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿لاًّصْحَابِ ٱلْيَمِينِ﴾.
That is: this is for the companions of the right.

farraa:39-40.t:
His saying here: ﴿ثُلَّةٌ مِّنَ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ وَثُلَّةٌ مِّنَ ٱلآخِرِينَ﴾.
He had said at the beginning of the sura: ﴿ثُلَّةٌ مِن الأوَّلين (13) وقليلٌ مِن الآخِرين﴾ (14). They mentioned that the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wept, and it was hard on them,
(namely) His saying ﴿وقليل من الآخرين﴾. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, revealed this: ﴿ثُلَّةٌ مِّنَ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ، وَثُلَّةٌ مِّنَ ٱلآخِرِينَ﴾. It is nominative as a new sentence (istiʾnāf); or, if you wish, you make it nominative (as a predicate), saying: and the companions of the right have two throngs: a throng of these and a throng of those. The meaning is: they are two groups, a group of these and a group of those.

farraa:43-43.t:
His saying: ﴿وَظِلٍّ مِّن يَحْمُومٍ﴾.
«اليحموم» is black smoke.

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَّ بَارِدٍ وَلاَ كَرِيمٍ﴾.
The proper construction is for it to be genitive, following what precedes it; similar to it are ﴿زَيْتُونَةٍ لا شرقيةٍ وَلا غَرْبِيَّةٍ﴾, and likewise ﴿وفاكهةٍ كثيرةٍ لا مقطُوعةٍ ولا ممنوعةٍ﴾. Had you made what follows nominative, it would have been correct Arabic speech. One of them recited to me:
وتُريكَ وجهاً كالصحيفةِ، لا * ظمآنُ مختلجٌ، ولا جَهْمُ
كعقيلةِ الدُّرِّ استضاءَ بها * محراب عرْش عزيزها العُجْمُ
(She shows you a face like a page, neither gaunt and twitching nor grim; like the choicest pearl, by which the non-Arabs lit up the sanctuary of their mighty one's throne.)
Another said:
ولقد أبِيت من الفتاة بمنزلٍ * فأبيت لا زانٍ ولا محروم
(I have spent the night in a place near the girl, and passed it neither an adulterer nor deprived.)
They begin anew with «لا»; but when they drop it, there is nothing for it but to make the end of the statement follow its beginning. The Arabs make «الكريم» follow anything from which they have negated a quality, intending blame by it. It is said: «أسمينٌ هذا؟» (Is this fat?), and you say: «ما هو بسمين ولا كريم» (it is neither fat nor fine); and «ما هذه الدار بواسعة ولا كريمة» (this house is neither spacious nor fine).

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ كَانُواْ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ مُتْرَفِينَ﴾.
Living in luxury in this world.

farraa:46-46.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكَانُواْ يُصِرُّونَ عَلَى ٱلْحِنثِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ﴾.
Associating partners with Allah (shirk): that is the great sin.

farraa:52-52.t:
His saying: ﴿لآكِلُونَ مِن شَجَرٍ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: «الآكلون من شجرة من زقوم». The meaning of «شجر» and «شجرة» is one, because when you say «أخذت من الشاء» (I took of the sheep), it is permissible whether you intend one or more than that.
«[Translator's note: «الآكلون» is as printed; presumably «لآكلون» is intended.]»

farraa:53-53.t:
Then He said: ﴿فَمَالِئُونَ مِنْهَا﴾.
From the tree. Had He said «فمالئون منه», since He did not mention «الشجرة» (in the singular), it would have been correct, taking «منه» to refer to «الشجر». And «الشجر» is made feminine, so «منها» is a pronoun referring to «الشجر»; «الشجر» is treated as feminine and masculine, like «الثمر».

farraa:54-54.t:
His saying: ﴿فَشَارِبُونَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلْحَمِيمِ﴾.
If you wish, it refers to «الشجر»; and if you wish, to the eating.

farraa:55-55.t:
His saying: ﴿فَشَارِبُونَ شُرْبَ ٱلْهِيمِ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ told us: al-Kisāʾī told me, from a man of Banū Umayya called Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Umawī, who said: I heard Ibn Jurayj read: "فشاربونَ شَرْب الهيم" with a fatḥa. He said: I mentioned that to Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, and he said: Is it not so? Has it not reached you that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Budayl ibn Warqāʾ al-Khuzāʿī to the people at Minā and said: "These are days of eating, drinking (shurb) and biʿāl."
Al-Farrāʾ said: «البِعال» means sexual intercourse. The rest of the readers give the shīn a ḍamma: "فشاربونَ شُرْب الهِيم". «الهيم» are camels struck by a disease so that they cannot quench their thirst with water; the singular is «أهيم» and the feminine «هيماء».
Some of the Arabs say «هائم», feminine «هائمة», then they pluralise it as «هيم», just as they said «عائط» and «عيط» (barren she-camels), and «حائل» and «حُول»; in meaning it is like «حائل / حُوْل», except that the ḍamma was dropped in «هيم» so that the yāʾ would not become a wāw. It is also said that «الهيم» is sand: He is saying that the people of the Fire will drink as soft sand (al-sihla) drinks. He said: al-Farrāʾ said: «الرملة» is itself «السهلة»; it is «سهلة» and «سِهلة».
«[Translator's note: the distinction between «سهلة» and «سهلة» at the end is lost in the unvowelled print (presumably «سَهْلة» and «سِهْلة»).]»

farraa:58-58.t:
His saying: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ مَّا تُمْنُونََ﴾.
He means: the drops of semen when they are cast into the wombs of women.
«[Translator's note: «قدفت» is as printed, evidently for «قذفت» (cast).]»

farraa:59-59.t:
His saying: ﴿أأنتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُ﴾.
Do you create those drops, or are We the Creators? It is said of a man «مَنى» and «أمنى» (he emitted semen), and «مَذى» and «أمذى» (he emitted pre-seminal fluid); «أمنى» is more frequent than «منى», and «مذى» more frequent than «أمذى».
«[Translator's note: «أكثى» is as printed, evidently for «أكثر» (more frequent).]»

farraa:63-64.t:
His saying: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتُم مَّا تَحْرُثُونَ.﴾.
That is: (do you) make it grow?

farraa:65-65.t:
His saying: ﴿فَظَلْتُمْ تَفَكَّهُونَ﴾.
You would wonder at what has befallen you in your crops. And it is said: the meaning of «تفكهون» is: you would regret.

farraa:66-66.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّا لَمُغْرَمُونَ﴾.
It is said: we are surely punished; and it is said: we are surely beset (by misfortune), and that is from their side.

farraa:70-70.t:
His saying: ﴿لَوْ نَشَآءُ جَعَلْنَاهُ أُجَاجاً﴾.
It is salty, bitter water of extreme bitterness.

farraa:73-73.t:
His saying: ﴿نَحْنُ جَعَلْنَاهَا تَذْكِرَةً وَمَتَاعاً لِّلْمُقْوِينَ﴾.
He means: a benefit for travellers when they halt in the «قِىّ» land, meaning the empty wilderness.

farraa:75-75.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلاَ أُقْسِمُ بِمَوَاقِعِ ٱلنُّجُومِ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ told us: Abū Laylā al-Sijistānī told me, from Abū Jarīr, the judge of Sijistān, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read: "فلا أُقْسِمَ بموقعِ النُّجومِ", and all the readers are for «مواقع».
Al-Farrāʾ told us: al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ told me, from Manṣūr, from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, tracing it back to ʿAbd Allāh as far as I know — al-Farrāʾ was unsure — [192/ب] he said: «فلا أقسم بموقع النجوم»; he said: by the muḥkam (firmly established) part of the Quran; and it used to come down to the Prophet ﷺ in instalments (nujūm).

farraa:76-76.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَقَسَمٌ لَّوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ﴾: this shows that it is the Quran.
And it is said: «فلا أقسم بموقع النجوم» means by the setting-places of the stars when they set.

farraa:79-79.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَّ يَمَسُّهُ إِلاَّ ٱلْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ told us: Ḥibbān told me, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: none touches that Preserved Tablet except the purified; he is saying: the angels, who have been purified of shirk. And it is said: «لا يمسه» means: none finds its taste and benefit except the purified, those who believe in it.

farraa:81-81.t: His saying: ﴿أَنتُمْ مُّدْهِنُونَ﴾: deniers and disbelievers; I have heard both.

farraa:82-82.t:
His saying: ﴿وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾.
It has come in the report: «تجعلون رزقكم» means: your thanks. In Arabic it is good to say: «جعلت زيارتى إياك أنك استخففت بى» (you made (the return for) my visiting you that you slighted me); the meaning then is: you made the reward of the visit to be rudeness. Likewise, you have made (your) thanks for provision to be denial.

farraa:83-83.t: His saying: ﴿فَلَوْلاَ إِذَا بَلَغَتِ ٱلْحُلْقُومَ﴾. He means: the soul at death.

farraa:84-84.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَنتُمْ حِينَئِذٍ تَنظُرُونَ﴾. He means: the family of the dying person who are with him,
looking at him. The Arabs address a group with an action as though they all did it, while only some of them are meant, whether absent or present; this is of that kind, like your saying to a group: «أنتم قتلتم فلاناً» (you killed so-and-so), when only one absent person killed him. Do you not see that you might say to the people in a mosque, if they had harmed a man by crowding: «Fear Allah, for you are harming the Muslims», and it would be correct?
In much of speech you admonish someone other than the doer. It is asked: where is the answer (jawāb) of the first «فلولا» and the answer of the one after it? The answer to that is that both were answered with one answer, which is «ترجعونها»; and the Arabs sometimes repeat two particles whose meaning is one. This is of that kind; and of it is: ﴿فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنّكُمْ مِنِّى هُدًى فَمن تَبِعَ هُداىَ فَلاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِم﴾: they were answered with one answer, though they are two conditional clauses (jazāʾān). And of that is His saying: ﴿لاَ تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِما أَتَوْا وَّيُحِبُّون أَنْ يُحْمَدُوا بِما لَمْ يَفْعَلُوا فَلا تَحْسَبَنَّهُم﴾,
and His saying: ﴿أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إذا مِتُّم وكُنتُم تُراباً وعِظَاماً أَنَّكُمْ مُخْرَجُون﴾; and it has been explained in another place than this.
«[Translator's note: «أنت قتلتم» is as printed, evidently for «أنتم قتلتم»; translated accordingly. «الموضوع» at the end is likewise as printed, for «الموضع» (place).]»

farraa:86-86.t:
His saying: ﴿غَيْرَ مَدِينِينَ﴾: (not) owned; and I have heard: (not) requited.
«[Translator's note: «مجزبين» is as printed, evidently for «مجزيين» (requited).]»

farraa:88-88.t: His saying: ﴿فَأَمَّآ إِن كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبِينَ﴾: of the people of the Garden of ʿAdn.

farraa:89-89.t:
﴿فَرَوْحٌ وَرَيْحَانٌ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ told us: an elder told me, from Ḥammād ibn Salama, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq, from ʿĀʾisha, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "فَروح وريحان"; and al-Ḥasan's reading is likewise. Al-Aʿmash, ʿĀṣim, al-Sulamī, the people of Medina and the rest of the readers (read) (فرَوحٌ), that is: rest in the grave. Whoever reads (فرُوحٌ) is saying: a life in which there is no death; and (وريحان): sustenance.
«[Translator's note: the vowelling of the reading attributed to ʿĀʾisha and al-Ḥasan is printed «فَروح», but the contrast drawn requires «فرُوح» (with ḍamma), which is how it is transmitted from them.]»

farraa:91-91.t:
His saying: ﴿فَسَلاَمٌ لَّكَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ ٱلْيَمِينِ﴾.
That is: that is granted to you, that you are of the companions of the right. «أنّ» was dropped while its meaning remains, as you say «أنت مصدّق مسافر عن قليل» (you are believed, travelling shortly) when he had said: «I am travelling shortly».
Likewise you find its meaning to be: you are believed that you are travelling; and its meaning (here) is: peace to you, you being of the companions of the right. It may also be like a prayer for him, as in your saying: «فسقيا لك من الرجال» (may you be watered, of all men!). If you make «السلام» nominative, it is a prayer.
And Allah knows best what is correct.

zajjaj:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿لا يُصَدَّعُونَ عَنْها ولا يُنْـزِفُونَ﴾ — its interpretation is: from drinking it they are not afflicted by the headache (ṣudāʿ) that afflicts the people of this world. ﴿وَلا يُنْـزِفُونَ﴾: they do not become intoxicated. "اَلنَّزِيفُ" is the drunk man; he is called "نَزِيفٌ" and "مَنزُوفٌ" only because his reason has been drained away (nazafa). It is also read: "وَلا يُنْزَفُونَ", meaning: their drink does not run out.

zajjaj:22-23.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَحُورٌ عِينٌ﴾ ﴿كَأمْثالِ اللُّؤْلُؤِ المَكْنُونِ﴾ — with the genitive (khafḍ); it has also been read with the nominative (rafʿ). Those who read it with the nominative disliked the genitive because it would be a conjunction (ʿaṭf) onto His saying: ﴿يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 17] ﴿بِأكْوابٍ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 18]; so they said: the ḥūr are not among the things that are carried round. But it is genitive on a basis other than what these people supposed, because the meaning of ﴿يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 17] is: they are blessed with this, and likewise they are blessed with the flesh of fowl, and likewise they are blessed with ḥūr ʿīn. Whoever read with the nominative has the better of the two options, because the meaning of ﴿يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 17] with these things is: that which has been established for them; so it is as if He said: "وَلَهم حُورٌ عِينٌ" (and they shall have ḥūr ʿīn). Similar to it, among what is construed according to the meaning (al-ḥaml ʿalā al-maʿnā), is the poet's saying:
بادَتْ وغُيِّرَ آيُهُنَّ مَعَ البِلى ∗∗∗ إلّا رَواكِدَ جَمْرُهُنَّ هَباءُ
(They have perished and their traces have been altered with decay, except the firm-set hearthstones whose embers are dust)
وَمُشَجَّجٌ أمّا سَواءُ قَذالُهُ ∗∗∗ فَبَدا وغَيَّرَ سارَهُ المِعْزاءُ
(and a battered tent-peg, whose head has become exposed, while the stony ground has altered the rest of it)
Because he said "إلّا رَواكِدَ", the meaning was: "بِها رَواكِدُ" (in it there are firm-set stones), so he construed "وَمُشَجَّجٌ" according to the meaning. It has also been read: "وَحُورًا عِينًا", with the accusative (naṣb), likewise by construal according to the meaning, because the meaning is: "they are given these things, they are given ḥūr ʿīn"; except that this reading differs from the Muṣḥaf, which is the Imām (the standard codex), and the people of knowledge dislike that anything be read which differs from the Imām. The meaning of "اَلْحُورُ" is: women of intense whiteness; and "اَلْعِينُ": women with large eyes, beautiful ones. The meaning of ﴿كَأمْثالِ اللُّؤْلُؤِ المَكْنُونِ﴾ is: like pearls when they come out of their shell and covering, unaltered by time and the changing conditions of use. By His saying ﴿كَأمْثالِ اللُّؤْلُؤِ﴾ He means only: in their purity and their lustre, like the purity and lustre of pearls.

zajjaj:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿جَزاءً بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ — accusative (manṣūb), a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is: "that is done for them as a recompense for their deeds". It is also possible that "جَزاءً" be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of ﴿يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 17] is: they are recompensed with a recompense for their deeds. This option is the one most grammarians hold.

zajjaj:26-26.t: His saying: ﴿إلا قِيلا سَلامًا سَلامًا﴾ — "قِيلًا" is accusative by His saying: "لا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيها لَغْوًا ولا تَأْثِيمًا، إلّا قِيلًا سَلامًا سَلامًا"; so the meaning is: "they hear nothing but a saying: سَلامًا سَلامًا". It is accusative on two counts. One of them is that it be a naʿt (adjective) of "قِيلًا", so that the meaning is: "they hear nothing but speech in which there is safety (yaslamu) from idle talk and sin". The second option is that ﴿سَلامًا﴾ be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), so that the meaning is: "they hear nothing in it except that some of them say to others: سَلامًا سَلامًا (peace, peace)". The evidence for this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿تَحِيَّتُهم فِيها سَلامٌ﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 23].

zajjaj:28-29.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِي سِدْرٍ مَخْضُودٍ﴾ ﴿وَطَلْحٍ مَنضُودٍ﴾ — "اَلْمَخْضُودُ" is that whose thorns have been stripped off. As for "اَلطَّلْحُ", it has come in the exegesis (tafsīr) that it is the banana tree. "اَلطَّلْحُ" is also the umm ghaylān tree (acacia), and it is possible that this tree is what is meant, because it has blossoms of a very fragrant scent; so they were addressed and promised the like of what they love, except that its superiority over what is in this world is like the superiority of everything else in Paradise over what is in this world.

zajjaj:30-30.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَظِلٍّ مَمْدُودٍ﴾ — its meaning is: complete and perpetual.

zajjaj:31-31.t: His saying: ﴿وَماءٍ مَسْكُوبٍ﴾ — what is meant is that it is water over which they take no toil; it pours out for them however they like.

zajjaj:35-35.t: His saying: ﴿إنّا أنْشَأْناهُنَّ إنْشاءً﴾ — He means the ḥūr: they were brought into being for the friends (awliyāʾ) of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and are not among those who underwent birth.

zajjaj:36-36.t: ﴿فَجَعَلْناهُنَّ أبْكارًا﴾: they have not been touched.

zajjaj:37-37.t: ﴿عُرُبًا﴾ — "اَلْعُرُبُ" are those who show love to their husbands.

zajjaj:39-40.t: His saying: ﴿ثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ ﴿وَثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الآخِرِينَ﴾ — its meaning, and Allah knows best, is: "a company of those who followed the Prophet ﷺ and saw him with their own eyes, and a company of those who believed in him and came after him."

zajjaj:43-43.t: His saying: ﴿وَظِلٍّ مِن يَحْمُومٍ﴾ — "اَلْيَحْمُومُ" is that which is intensely black. It has been said that it is intensely black smoke; and it has been said that ﴿وَظِلٍّ مِن يَحْمُومٍ﴾ means: of a fire with which they are punished. The evidence for this is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَهم مِن فَوْقِهِمْ ظُلَلٌ مِنَ النّارِ ومِن تَحْتِهِمْ ظُلَلٌ﴾ [al-Zumar: 16]; except that here it is described as intensely black.

zajjaj:46-46.t: ﴿وَكانُوا يُصِرُّونَ عَلى الحِنْثِ العَظِيمِ﴾ — it has been said in the exegesis: "اَلْحِنْثُ" is shirk (associating partners with Allah); and it has been said: "upon the great sin". It is, and Allah knows best, shirk and disbelief in the resurrection, because in the Quran there is evidence of that, namely: ﴿وَأقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أيْمانِهِمْ لا يَبْعَثُ اللَّهُ مَن يَمُوتُ بَلى وعْدًا عَلَيْهِ حَقًّا﴾ [al-Naḥl: 38]. So this, and Allah knows best, is their persistence in the great ḥinth.

zajjaj:55-55.t: ﴿فَشارِبُونَ شُرْبَ الهِيمِ﴾ — it is also read: "شَرْبَ الهِيمِ". "اَلشَّرْبُ" is the maṣdar (verbal noun) and "اَلشُّرْبُ" is the noun; it has also been said that al-shurb is likewise a maṣdar. "اَلْهِيمُ" are thirsty camels.

zajjaj:56-56.t: His saying: ﴿هَذا نُـزُلُهم يَوْمَ الدِّينِ﴾ — that is: this is their nourishment on the Day of Recompense, that is, the day they are recompensed for their deeds.

zajjaj:58-58.t: His saying: ﴿أفَرَأيْتُمْ ما تُمْنُونَ﴾ — that is: the semen (manī) that comes from you, from which the child comes into being. One says: "أمْنى الرَّجُلُ، يُمَنِي" and "مَنى، يَمْنِي"; so on this basis "تَمْنُونَ" with fatḥa on the tāʾ would be permissible, but I know of no one who read it so; so do not read it so unless a transmission is established.

zajjaj:59-59.t: His saying: ﴿أأنْتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُ أمْ نَحْنُ الخالِقُونَ﴾ — He argued against them concerning the resurrection by His power to originate creation, as He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَضَرَبَ لَنا مَثَلا ونَسِيَ خَلْقَهُ قالَ مَن يُحْيِي العِظامَ وهي رَمِيمٌ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 78] ﴿قُلْ يُحْيِيها الَّذِي أنْشَأها أوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وهو بِكُلِّ خَلْقٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 79].

zajjaj:60-61.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿نَحْنُ قَدَّرْنا بَيْنَكُمُ المَوْتَ وما نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ﴾ ﴿عَلى أنْ نُبَدِّلَ أمْثالَكم ونُنْشِئَكم في ما لا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — that is: if We wished to create a creation other than you, no one would outstrip Us, nor would that escape Us.
His saying: ﴿وَنُنْشِئَكم في ما لا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — that is: if We wished to make apes and swine out of you, We would not be outstripped, nor would that escape Us.

zajjaj:62-62.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ النَّشْأةَ الأُولى فَلَوْلا تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ — that is: you have known the origination of creation, so why have you denied the resurrection? The meaning of "لَوْلا تَذَكَّرُونَ" is: will you not then remember (hallā tadhakkarūn)?

zajjaj:65-65.t: His saying: ﴿فَظَلْتُمْ تَفَكَّهُونَ﴾ — that is: if We made what you sow into debris (ḥuṭām), that is, rendered it void until it is broken to pieces, with no wheat in it nor anything of what you sow, ﴿فَظَلْتُمْ تَفَكَّهُونَ﴾, that is: you would remain regretting. "فَظِلْتُمْ تَفَكَّهُونَ", with kasra on the ẓāʾ, is also permissible.

zajjaj:66-66.t: His saying: ﴿إنّا لَمُغْرَمُونَ﴾ — that is: they say: we have suffered loss and our crop is gone; ﴿بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 67].

zajjaj:69-69.t: His saying: ﴿أأنْتُمْ أنْـزَلْتُمُوهُ مِنَ المُزْنِ أمْ نَحْنُ المُنْـزِلُونَ﴾ — it (al-muzn) is the clouds; its singular is "مُزْنَةٌ" and its plural is "مُزْنٌ".

zajjaj:70-70.t: His saying: ﴿لَوْ نَشاءُ جَعَلْناهُ أُجاجًا﴾ — "اَلْأُجاجُ" is salt water that cannot possibly be drunk at all. ﴿فَلَوْلا تَشْكُرُونَ﴾: its meaning is "فَهَلّا" (will you not then).

zajjaj:71-71.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أفَرَأيْتُمُ النّارَ الَّتِي تُورُونَ﴾ — its meaning is: you strike fire. You say: "وَرى الزَّنْدُ يَرِي، ورْيًا، فَهو وارٍ" when fire is struck from the fire-stick (zand), and "أوْرَيْتُ النّارَ" when you have struck it. The Arabs strike fire with the zand and the zanda, which are pieces of wood rubbed one against the other so that fire comes out of them. So He said: ﴿أأنْتُمْ أنْشَأْتُمْ شَجَرَتَها أمْ نَحْنُ المُنْشِئُونَ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 72] ﴿نَحْنُ جَعَلْناها تَذْكِرَةً ومَتاعًا لِلْمُقْوِينَ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 73], that is: when the beholder sees it he remembers Hell and the punishment he fears, and so he remembers Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and seeks refuge with Him from it. As for the meaning of "مَتاعًا لِّلْمُقْوِينَ": "اَلْمُقْوِي" is the one who alights in al-qiwāʾ, which is empty land. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, mentioned everything that points to His oneness, and the favours He bestowed on them in creating them and nourishing them with what they eat and drink, which points to His power and His uniqueness; then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ العَظِيمِ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 74], that is: declare Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, free (of every imperfection).

zajjaj:75-75.t: ﴿فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِمَواقِعِ النُّجُومِ﴾ — its meaning is "أُقْسِمُ" (I swear), and "لا" entered as tawkīd (emphasis), as He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِئَلا يَعْلَمَ أهْلُ الكِتابِ﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 29], whose meaning is: "that the People of the Book may know". The mawāqiʿ of the stars are the places where they set, as He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ المَشارِقِ والمَغارِبِ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 40]. It has also been said that by the mawāqiʿ of the stars (nujūm) is meant "the instalments (nujūm) of the Quran", because it used to be sent down upon the Prophet ﷺ in instalments, one thing after another; and the evidence for this view is: ﴿وَإنَّهُ لَقَسَمٌ لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 76] ﴿إنَّهُ لَقُرْآنٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 77].

zajjaj:78-78.t: His saying: ﴿فِي كِتابٍ مَكْنُونٍ﴾ — that is: guarded in heaven, in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ).

zajjaj:79-79.t: His saying: ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ إلا المُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ — by this are meant the angels: none touches it in the Preserved Tablet except the angels. It is also read: "اَلْمُطَهِّرُونَ", which is a rare reading, and it has two interpretations. One of them: "those who have purified themselves of sins"; the second is that it be "those who purify others".

zajjaj:80-80.t: His saying: ﴿تَنْـزِيلٌ مِن رَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾ — it is a ṣifa (adjective) of His saying "كَرِيمٌ"; and if you wish, it is nominative (marfūʿ) on the reading: "هُوَ تَنْزِيلٌ مِن رَبِّ العالَمِينَ" (it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds).

zajjaj:81-81.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أفَبِهَذا الحَدِيثِ أنْتُمْ مُدْهِنُونَ﴾ — that is: "is it the Quran that you deny?" "اَلْمُدْهِنُ" is the one who temporises (al-mudāhin), and the lying hypocrite.

zajjaj:82-82.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكم أنَّكم تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾ — they used to say: "we have been given rain by such-and-such a star (nawʾ)", and would not ascribe the watering to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. So it was said to them: do you make your provision — that is, your thanks for what you have been provided — denial? It has been read: "وَتَجْعَلُونَ شُكْرَكم أنَّكُمْ", but it ought not to be read so, because it differs from the Muṣḥaf. They have said that the interpretation of "رِزْقَكُمْ" here is thanks (al-shukr), and they have transmitted that one says "وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقِي" in the sense of "شُكْرِي" (my thanks); but this is not sound. Rather, the wording of His saying ﴿وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكم أنَّكم تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾ points to the meaning "وَتَجْعَلُونَ شُكْرَكم أنَّكم تُكَذِّبُونَ", that is: you make the thanks for your provision that you say "we have been given rain by such-and-such a star", and so you lie in that.

zajjaj:83-83.t: His saying: ﴿فَلَوْلا إذا بَلَغَتِ الحُلْقُومَ﴾ — He means: "when the soul (al-rūḥ) reaches the throat".

zajjaj:84-84.t: ﴿وَأنْتُمْ حِينَئِذٍ تَنْظُرُونَ﴾ — that is: you, O family of the dying man, in that state see him having reached the point where his soul departs.

zajjaj:85-85.t: ﴿وَنَحْنُ أقْرَبُ إلَيْهِ مِنكم ولَكِنْ لا تُبْصِرُونَ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that no one dies until he knows whether he is of the people of Paradise or of the people of the Fire.

zajjaj:87-87.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَرْجِعُونَها إنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ﴾ — its meaning is: why do you not bring back the soul, if you are not "مَدِينِينَ", that is, not owned and governed, having no power over life and death? So why not, if you are as you claimed — like that saying of yours which has come in the Quran: ﴿الَّذِينَ قالُوا لإخْوانِهِمْ وقَعَدُوا لَوْ أطاعُونا ما قُتِلُوا قُلْ فادْرَءُوا عَنْ أنْفُسِكُمُ المَوْتَ إنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 168], as He said: ﴿أوْ كانُوا غُزًّى لَوْ كانُوا عِنْدَنا ما ماتُوا وما قُتِلُوا﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 156]? So the meaning is: "if you are able to postpone an appointed term, why then do you not bring back the soul when it reaches the throat, and why do you not avert death from yourselves?"

zajjaj:88-89.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأمّا إنْ كانَ مِنَ المُقَرَّبِينَ﴾ ﴿فَرَوْحٌ ورَيْحانٌ﴾ — with fatḥa on the rāʾ in "رَوْحٌ"; its meaning is: then rest and coolness; and rayḥān is provision (rizq). The poet said:
سَلامُ الإلَهِ ورَيْحانُهُ ∗∗∗ ورَحْمَتُهُ وسَماءٌ دُرَرْ
(The peace of God and His provision (rayḥān), and His mercy, and a sky pouring abundant rain)
It has also been transmitted as "فَرُوحٌ", with ḍamma on the rāʾ, and its interpretation is: "then perpetual life with no death after it; and rayḥān is provision". It is also possible that "رَيْحانٌ" here be a greeting for the people of Paradise. The grammarians agree that the origin of "رَيْحانٌ" in the language is "رَيِّحانٌ", from the roots with wāw (dhawāt al-wāw); so the origin is "رَيْوِحانٌ": the wāw was changed to yāʾ and the first (yāʾ) was assimilated (udghimat) into it, so it became "رَيِّحانٌ"; then it was lightened, just as they said "مَيْتٌ" for "مَيِّتٌ". Doubling (tashdīd) is not permissible in "رَيْحانٌ" except as a far-fetched option, because alif and nūn have been added to it, so it was lightened by dropping the (second) yāʾ, and the lightening was made obligatory for it. Its nominative (rafʿ) is on the meaning: "as for him, if the deceased is of those brought near, then for him there is rawḥ and rayḥān".

zajjaj:90-91.t: His saying: ﴿وَأمّا إنْ كانَ مِن أصْحابِ اليَمِينِ﴾ ﴿فَسَلامٌ لَكَ مِن أصْحابِ اليَمِينِ﴾ — He has already made clear what belongs to the Companions of the Right at the beginning of the sūra. The meaning of ﴿فَسَلامٌ لَكَ مِن أصْحابِ اليَمِينِ﴾ is that you see in them the safety (salāma) you love, and you have already learned the recompense prepared for them.

zajjaj:92-93.t: His saying: ﴿وَأمّا إنْ كانَ مِنَ المُكَذِّبِينَ الضّالِّينَ﴾ ﴿فَنُـزُلٌ مِن حَمِيمٍ﴾ — it is read "فَنُزْلٌ", with the lightened form and with the heavy form. Its meaning is: "then nourishment of scalding water and roasting in Hellfire", that is: abiding in Hellfire. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that Hellfire here is for the deniers who go astray.

zajjaj:95-95.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ هَذا لَهو حَقُّ اليَقِينِ﴾ — that is: this which We have narrated to you in this sūra of accounts, and what Allah has prepared for His friends and His enemies, and what has been mentioned of what points to His oneness, is certainty, the truth of certainty; just as you say: "إنَّ زَيْدًا لَعالِمٌ حَقُّ عالِمٍ" (Zayd is a scholar, truly a scholar) and "إنَّهُ لَلْعالِمُ حَقُّ العالِمِ" (he is the scholar, truly the scholar), when you intensify the emphasis.

zajjaj:96-96.t:
His saying: ﴿فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ العَظِيمِ﴾ — that is: declare Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, free of evil, because the meaning of "سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ" is declaring Allah free of evil. Thus it has come from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and thus the lexicographers explain it: "the freedom (barāʾa) of Allah from evil". Sībawayh cited in this sense:
أقُولُ لِما جاءَ في فَخْرِهِ ∗∗∗ سُبْحانَ مِن عَلْقَمَةَ الفاجِرِ
(I say, when his boasting reached me: I am quit of ʿAlqama the wicked!)
That is: I declare myself quit of him.

Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إذا وقَعَتِ الواقِعَةُ﴾: of everything that comes which was being expected one says "qad waqaʿa" (it has occurred). You say "qad waqaʿa l-amru" (the matter has occurred), like your saying "qad jāʾa l-amru" (the matter has come). "اَلْواقِعَةُ" here is the Hour and the Resurrection.

zajjaj:10-11.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿والسّابِقُونَ السّابِقُونَ﴾ ﴿أُولَئِكَ المُقَرَّبُونَ﴾: its meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "The foremost, those foremost in the obedience of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and in affirming the truth of His prophets." The first "اَلسّابِقُونَ" is nominative by ibtidāʾ (as mubtadaʾ, subject), the second is tawkīd (emphasis), and the khabar (predicate) is ﴿أُولَئِكَ المُقَرَّبُونَ﴾. Then He told where their abode is, saying: ﴿فِي جَنّاتِ النَّعِيمِ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 12]. And it may be that the first "اَلسّابِقُونَ" is nominative as the mubtadaʾ and its khabar is the second "اَلسّابِقُونَ", so that the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "Those foremost in the obedience of Allah are the foremost to the mercy of Allah", and ﴿أُولَئِكَ المُقَرَّبُونَ﴾ would be part of their description.

zajjaj:13-14.t: And His saying: ﴿ثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ ﴿وَقَلِيلٌ مِنَ الآخِرِينَ﴾: "ثُلَّةٌ" is nominative in the sense of "They are a thulla"; "اَلثُّلَّةُ" is a group. This — and Allah knows best — is the meaning of ﴿ثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الأوَّلِينَ﴾, that is: a group of those who saw the prophets with their own eyes and believed them; for those who saw all the prophets and believed them are more numerous than those who saw the Prophet, peace be upon him. That is His saying — in the story of Yūnus —: ﴿وَأرْسَلْناهُ إلى مِائَةِ ألْفٍ أوْ يَزِيدُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 147] ﴿فَآمَنُوا فَمَتَّعْناهم إلى حِينٍ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 148]: these are besides all the others who believed in all the prophets among those who saw them and believed them. And "اَلثُّلَّةُ" may be in the sense of "a few of the former and a few of the latter", because the derivation of al-thulla is from "the piece (al-qiṭʿa)": "al-thall" is breaking and cutting, and "al-thulla" is like a party (fiʾa) or a faction (firqa).

zajjaj:15-16.t:
And His saying: ﴿عَلى سُرُرٍ مَوْضُونَةٍ﴾ ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلَيْها مُتَقابِلِينَ﴾: "مُتَّكِئِينَ" and "مُتَقابِلِينَ" are both accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "Those are the ones brought near, in the gardens of bliss, in this state." "اَلسُّرُرُ" is the plural of "سَرِيرٌ" (couch), like "كَثِيبٌ" and "كُثُبٌ". The meaning of "مُتَقابِلِينَ" is: they look at one another's faces, and look at the backs of one another's heads «[Translator's note: so in the source (ويَنْظُرُ في أقْفاءِ بَعْضٍ); the sense presumably intended is "and do not look at the backs of one another's heads".]». They are described, along with their bliss, by good companionship, refined character and purity of affection. Of this is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنَـزَعْنا ما في صُدُورِهِمْ مِن غِلٍّ إخْوانًا عَلى سُرُرٍ مُتَقابِلِينَ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 47]. It has come in the exegesis that "مَوْضُونَةٍ" means marmūla, and the meaning of "مَرْمُولَةٌ" is: woven, like the weaving of coats of mail; and it has come in the exegesis that they are of gold. An example of "مَوْضُونَةٌ" is the saying of al-Aʿshā:
؎وَمِن نَسْجِ داوُدَ مَوْضُونَةٌ ∗∗∗ يُساقُ بِها الحَيُّ عِيرًا فَعِيرا
(And close-woven [mail] of David's weaving, which the tribe carries along, caravan after caravan.)

zajjaj:17-18.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ﴾ ﴿بِأكْوابٍ وأبارِيقَ﴾: "اَلْأكْوابُ" are vessels that have no handles and no spouts, and "اَلْإبْرِيقُ" is what has a spout and a handle. ﴿وَكَأْسٍ مِن مَعِينٍ﴾: "اَلْكَأْسُ" is the vessel with drink in it; if there is no drink in it, it is not a kaʾs.
And His saying: ﴿مِن مَعِينٍ﴾: its meaning is: of wine flowing from springs.

zajjaj:2-2.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِها كاذِبَةٌ﴾, that is: nothing repels it, as you say "qad ḥamala fulānun lā yukadhdhibu" (So-and-so charged without flinching), that is: nothing repels his charge. "كاذِبَةٌ" is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like your saying "ʿāfāhu llāhu ʿāfiyatan" (Allah granted him well-being) and "ʿāqabahu ʿāqibatan" (He punished him); and likewise "kadhdhaba kādhibatan". These are nouns standing in the position of maṣdars.

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿خافِضَةٌ رافِعَةٌ﴾: the meaning is that it lowers the people of sin and raises the people of obedience. As for ﴿خافِضَةٌ رافِعَةٌ﴾, the reading is with the nominative; the accusative is permissible, but no imam among the Readers read it so, though it has been transmitted from al-Yazīdī «[Translator's note: the source has الزيدي, "al-Zaydī"; the companion of Abū ʿAmr is known as al-Yazīdī.]», the companion of Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ. Whoever reads the nominative — and that is the proper way — the meaning is: "It is lowering, raising." And whoever reads the accusative does so in one of two ways. One of them is: "When the Event occurs, lowering, raising", as a ḥāl (circumstantial). And it may be with "تَقَعُ" implied, the meaning being: "When it occurs, it occurs lowering, raising", as a ḥāl from the implied "تَقَعُ".

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying: ﴿إذا رُجَّتِ الأرْضُ رَجًّا﴾: the position of "إذا" is accusative; the meaning is: "When it occurs at that time." The accusative may also be on the basis of "it occurs when the earth is shaken with a shaking". The meaning of ﴿رُجَّتِ﴾ is: it is moved with violent motion and quaked.

zajjaj:5-5.t: ﴿وَبُسَّتِ الجِبالُ بَسًّا﴾: "بُسَّتْ" means: moistened and mixed; and "بُسَّتْ" also means: driven along.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
﴿فَكانَتْ هَباءً مُنْبَثًّا﴾: dust. Similar to it is ﴿وَسُيِّرَتِ الجِبالُ فَكانَتْ سَرابًا﴾ [al-Nabaʾ: 20]. An example of "mixed and moistened" is the poet's saying:
؎لا تَخْبِزا خَبْزًا وبُسّا بَسّا
(Do not bake bread, you two, but mix [the flour] a mixing.)
And an example of "driven and moving along" is his saying:
؎وانْبَسَّ حَيّاتُ الكَثِيبِ الأهْيَلِ
(And the snakes of the shifting sand-dune crept along.)

zajjaj:7-7.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكُنْتُمْ أزْواجًا ثَلاثَةً﴾, that is: three kinds. Kinds that go together with one another are called "أزْواجٌ", just as a pair of khuffs (leather socks) is called "zawjān".

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying: ﴿فَأصْحابُ المَيْمَنَةِ ما أصْحابُ المَيْمَنَةِ﴾ is nominative by ibtidāʾ (as mubtadaʾ, subject); the meaning is: "And the companions of the right — what are they?! What sort of thing are they?! ﴿وَأصْحابُ المَشْأمَةِ ما أصْحابُ المَشْأمَةِ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 9] — what sort of thing are they?!" This wording follows in Arabic the course of exclamation of wonder (taʿajjub), and from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, in addressing His servants it follows the course of that by which a matter is made great in their eyes. Similar to it are ﴿الحاقَّةُ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 1] ﴿ما الحاقَّةُ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 2] and ﴿القارِعَةُ﴾ [al-Qāriʿa: 1] ﴿ما القارِعَةُ﴾ [al-Qāriʿa: 2]. The meaning of "أصْحابُ المَيْمَنَةِ" is: the companions of the right hand, and "أصْحابُ المَشْأمَةِ": the companions of the left hand. The companions of the right are the people of the lofty rank, and the companions of the left are the people of the low, base rank.
